text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Singapore's search for alternative sources of water supply a top priority of Government and recent events have added urgency to it, Minister for Trade and Industry Lee Yock Suan tells Parliament.
- Singapore ranked second freest economy in the world, with its rapid growth and high level of per capita income cited as illustrating potential for growth in economically free environment.
- Driver tries to crash station wagon through police cordon around Chinese Embassy in Tokyo in a protest on eighth anniversary of China's Tiananmen Square crackdown.
- Apple Computer will lay off another 250 workers in Singapore as it stops making printed circuit boards (PCBs) at Ang Mo Kio plant and focuses on systems assembly.
- Shares of DBS Land fall 24 cents or 4.8 percent to close at Singapore $4.76 after property group says placing out 91.9 million new shares on Tuesday at Singapore $4.75 apiece.
- CAM International Holdings fires chief financial officer Ng Chee Tiong and says will take steps to remove him as executive director at next general meeting.
- In a rare case of its kind, six persons arrested in Hong Kong for allegedly inflating circulation of "The Hongkong Standard" newspaper and its Sunday edition to deceive advertisers.

- National Development Minister Lim Hng Kiang rejects calls to impose increased Housing Development Board resale levy on a sliding scale, and leaves open question whether further changes to housing policies on the cards.
- Singapore government investing about Singapore $135 million to buy a 5 percent stake in tycoon Robert Kuok's Hongkong-based hotel chain, Shangri-La Asia.

- Amcol executive directors Ng Chee Kheong and Llyod Lochra had asked businessman Peter Tay to find an investor for a Mauritian joint venture while trying at the same time to push the project through the company, it was claimed in court.
- United Industrial Corp (UIC) and Singapore Land's new suburban shopping complex, West Mall, is already 75 percent leased ahead of its opening towards the middle of next year.
